items.title_en: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
items.title_zh: GPT-6-Astra 是否已实现具身智能？
items.abstract_en: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., π0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.
items.abstract_zh: GPT-6-Astra 在机器人操作与导航上的表现，挑战了为单一任务和单一本体定制专用模型的传统范式。本报告在覆盖桌面操作、人形机器人、移动平台与灵巧手的 12 个代表性基准上进行大规模评测：在允许上下文学习（ICL）并大幅放宽执行步数的统一协议下，它取得了前所未有的性能。研究还发现，高层“System 2”推理器与低层“System 1”控制器的闭环协同代价高昂但有效；在 8 种真实机器人配置上的部署实验则暴露出明显差距：ICL 所需的机器人示范采集成本高，且受物理条件限制，难以用更长执行时间换取更高成功率。作者据此提出五项待改进方向，并构想以真实需求驱动、不提供域内示范、按持续运行的世界时钟评判的下一代具身基准原型。
items.highlight_zh: GPT-6-Astra 在 12 个具身基准上刷新性能，真实部署仍存明显差距
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：通用大模型能否直接充当机器人的“大脑”，取代为每个任务、每种机器人单独训练专用策略？
方法：作者以 GPT-6-Astra 为对象做了三类实验。①在 12 个代表性基准（桌面操作、人形、移动平台、灵巧手）上做大规模评测，采用统一协议，允许模型从训练集示范中做上下文学习（ICL），并把允许的执行步数大幅放宽；②把它当作高层“System 2”推理器，与低层“System 1”控制器（如 π0.5）组成闭环智能体框架；③在 8 种真实机器人配置上做部署测试。
结果：在宽松协议下，GPT-6-Astra 取得前所未有的表现，说明其通用操作与导航能力已跨越某个门槛。代价同样明显：闭环协同虽有效却昂贵；真机上 ICL 所需的机器人示范采集成本高，且受物理约束，无法靠“多花时间执行”换取更高成功率。
作者列出五个待改进方向：ICL 的泛化性、成本与执行时间、物理状态核验、不可逆失败后的恢复、长时程任务进度的保持。
为何重要：文中还提出下一代具身基准原型——任务取自真实需求、不提供域内示范、并用一个在智能体“思考”时仍持续走动的世界时钟来计时评分。这直指当前基准的软肋：允许无限思考时间与域内示范的评测，会高估机器人在真实世界中的可用性。

rm.usage: 一篇关于通用具身智能基准的评测报告，讨论 VLM 高层推理与底层控制的闭环，以及示范数据采集成本。对 RoboMaster 各具体任务（自瞄、导航、决策）没有可直接落地的算法，只能作为「大模型能否直接驱动机器人」的宏观参考，关联很弱。

items.title_en: Simultaneous Force and Motion Control in Generalised Coordinates
items.title_zh: 广义坐标下的力与运动同时控制
items.abstract_en: Robot manipulators often come into contact with rigid objects when performing work. This imposes physical constraints on their motion. Simultaneous force & motion control was developed to regulate contact forces commensurate with these constraints, whilst projecting motion control in to the orthogonal, unconstrained directions. This is typically formulated in the task coordinates, i.e. operational space, then mapped to joint torques to command the robot. However, most constraints on the robot control, such as joint limits, collision avoidance, singularity avoidance, etc. are naturally expressed in generalised coordinates (joint space). Thus, formulating the control problem in task space makes it difficult to guarantee control feasibility. In this paper Gauss' principle of least constraint is used to solve the control as a quadratic programming (QP) problem in generalised coordinates. It is shown that the theoretical solution to this problem produces the correct constrained dynamics for accurate contact force control. Moreover, inequality constraints may be appended to ensure feasibility and safety. Simulation results were conducted in MuJoCo and compared to the operational space formulation. The proposed method is able to simultaneously maintain a desired contact force, minimise trajectory tracking error, and adhere to practical inequality constraints.
items.abstract_zh: 机械臂作业时常接触刚性物体，运动因此受到物理约束。力与运动同时控制正是为在约束方向上调节接触力、并将运动控制投影到正交的无约束方向而提出，通常在任务坐标（操作空间）中建模再映射为关节力矩。然而关节限位、避碰、奇异回避等控制约束天然定义在广义坐标（关节空间）中，任务空间建模难以保证控制可行性。本文利用高斯最小约束原理，把控制问题写成广义坐标下的二次规划（QP）。理论分析表明，其解可给出正确的约束动力学，实现精确接触力控制；同时可附加不等式约束以保证可行性与安全性。在 MuJoCo 仿真中与操作空间法对比，所提方法能同时维持期望接触力、最小化轨迹跟踪误差，并满足实际不等式约束。
items.highlight_zh: 用高斯最小约束原理在关节空间把力/运动控制解成 QP，兼顾可行性
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：机械臂接触刚性物体时，既要控制接触力又要控制运动。经典做法是在任务空间（操作空间）中求解，再映射成关节力矩。但关节限位、避碰、奇异回避这些真正的限制条件都天然写在关节空间里，因此在任务空间中求解很难保证控制可行，可能解出违反约束的指令。
方法：作者改用高斯最小约束原理（Gauss' principle of least constraint），把力与运动同时控制直接建模为广义坐标（关节空间）下的二次规划（QP）问题；不等式约束（如关节限位）可以直接加入 QP，以保证可行性与安全性。
结果：理论分析表明，该 QP 的解能给出正确的约束动力学，从而精确控制接触力；在 MuJoCo 仿真中与操作空间法对比，所提方法能同时维持期望接触力、最小化轨迹跟踪误差，并满足实际不等式约束。
为何重要：把约束放回其本来的坐标，使高层任务目标与底层安全、可行性约束在同一优化中统一处理。对需要频繁接触作业的机械臂（装配、打磨、抓取）有直接的工程价值，也为后续加入更多硬约束留出了统一接口。
items.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, submitted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2027

rm.usage: 把力/运动同时控制写成广义坐标下的 QP，可附加关节限位、避碰、奇异回避等不等式约束。工程机器人装配（安装 42mm 发射机构、能量单元）正需要带接触力调节与安全约束的机械臂控制，可把该 QP 框架直接用于工程臂的装配对接环节。

items.title_en: Pedicel-Targeted Strawberry Harvesting via Imitation Learning on a Low-Cost Teleoperated Robotic Arm
items.title_zh: 基于模仿学习的低成本遥操作机械臂花梗靶向草莓采摘
items.abstract_en: Precise pedicel-targeted grasping in strawberry harvesting remains a critical bottleneck due to the pedicel's small diameter (1.3-3 mm), color similarity with surrounding foliage, and precise force control required for clean abscission zone detachment. As a market-grade crop, strawberry aesthetic value makes bruise-free pedicel detachment essential over direct fruit grasping. Classical approaches struggle to unify vision models, motion planning, and contact manipulation into a robust framework, particularly in occluded canopy environments. Therefore, this work presents a visuomotor imitation learning pipeline for pedicel-targeted strawberry harvesting that unifies perception, motion planning, and contact manipulation from collecting human teleoperation demonstrations, training an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy with a ResNet-50 visual backbone, and deploying the learned policy autonomously on a Jetson AGX Orin edge platform at 15 Hz. The trained policy achieved consistent loss convergence from 2.84 to 0.091 over 100K gradient steps on 130 demonstrations. We have also established a reproducible open-source pipeline with publicly released dataset and model weights for the agricultural robotics community. Full dataset is available at, https://huggingface.co/datasets/nitindominicrai/strawberry_pedicel_grasp_teleoperation and trained policy at, https://huggingface.co/nitindominicrai/act_strawberry_pedicel. To replicate this work, all code, configurations, and deployment instructions are publicly available at, https://github.com/nitin-dominic/autonomous_strawberry_pedicel_harvesting.
items.abstract_zh: 草莓采摘中花梗直径仅 1.3–3 mm、与周围枝叶颜色相近，且需精确力控才能干净切断离层，使花梗靶向抓取成为关键瓶颈；作为商品性作物，无损伤的花梗分离比直接抓取果实更重要。传统方法难以把视觉模型、运动规划与接触操作统一为鲁棒框架，在遮挡冠层中尤为困难。为此，本文提出视觉运动模仿学习流程：采集人类遥操作示范，训练以 ResNet-50 为视觉骨干的 ACT（Action Chunking with Transformers）策略，并在 Jetson AGX Orin 边缘平台以 15 Hz 自主部署。130 条示范、10 万梯度步内损失由 2.84 收敛至 0.091。数据集、模型权重与代码均已公开，形成可复现的开源流程。
items.highlight_zh: 用 ACT 模仿学习让低成本机械臂在边缘端 15 Hz 自主采草莓花梗
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：草莓若直接抓果实容易压伤、影响商品价值，因此应抓住直径仅 1.3–3 mm 的花梗，并在离层处干净分离。但花梗极细、颜色与枝叶相近、常被遮挡，还需精确控力，传统“视觉模型＋运动规划＋接触控制”的分模块方案在遮挡冠层中很难稳定整合。
方法：作者采用端到端模仿学习。先用低成本遥操作机械臂采集 130 条人类示范，训练 ACT（Action Chunking with Transformers）策略，视觉骨干为 ResNet-50；再把学到的策略部署到 Jetson AGX Orin 边缘平台，以 15 Hz 自主运行。
结果：训练在 10 万梯度步内使损失由 2.84 稳定降到 0.091，说明策略能较好地拟合示范。作者同时完整开源了数据集、模型权重、代码与部署说明，形成可复现的流程。
为何重要：一是把感知、规划与接触操作统一进一个可学习策略，绕开了模块化管线在细小目标上难以对接的问题；二是验证了低成本硬件加边缘算力即可跑通精细农业操作；三是开源降低了农业机器人社区复现与横向比较的门槛。需要说明的是，文中主要报告训练收敛与部署流程，尚未给出大规模田间采摘成功率的统计。
items.comment: 4 pages, 3 figures. This paper was peer-reviewed and accepted in the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), "From Innovation to Adoption: Hardware, AI, Policy, and Funding Challenges in Agricultural Robotics Workshop," Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, 2026

rm.usage: 提供了一条「遥操作采集示范 → ACT 视觉运动策略 → Jetson 边缘 15Hz 部署」的完整开源流程。工程机器人视觉装配可借鉴这套模仿学习流水线，用少量人工示范快速教会机械臂抓取和对接模块，降低手工编程成本。

items.title_en: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
items.title_zh: FastVLA：面向高效视觉-语言-动作模型的任务条件化与时间自适应视觉 Token 压缩
items.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts end-to-end latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.
items.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型是通用机器人操作的有力范式，但闭环部署常受推理效率限制：每个时间步都要把高分辨率、多视角图像编码成数百个视觉 token，主导了 Transformer 计算与延迟。基于注意力的 token 压缩对 VLA 控制并不简单：决策关键 token 由任务而非通用视觉显著性决定；且 token 预算随步数大幅波动，静态指标与固定预算会浪费算力或丢弃控制关键 token。本文提出 FastVLA——免训练、任务感知、时间自适应的视觉 token 压缩框架：每步用任务到视觉的注意力给 token 打分，并以逆 Simpson 指标衡量重要性分布均匀度、结合在线滑窗校准自适应设定压缩率。在 OpenVLA、OpenVLA-OFT、CogACT 与 LIBERO、SIMPLER 及真实 Franka Research 3 上验证：仿真中 LLM 主干 FLOPs 降低 35–59%、动作延迟降低 9–32%（1.09–1.46 倍加速）且成功率保持；真机端到端延迟降低 20%（1.25 倍加速）。
items.highlight_zh: 免训练、随任务自适应的视觉 token 压缩，真机延迟降 20%
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：VLA（视觉-语言-动作）模型是通用机器人操作的有力范式，但闭环部署受推理速度拖累：每个控制步都要把高分辨率、多视角图像编码成数百个视觉 token，这些 token 主导了 Transformer 的计算量与延迟。
难点：直接照搬视觉领域的 token 压缩行不通。①哪些 token 对决策关键取决于当前任务指令，而不是通用视觉显著性——背景里高对比的物体未必有用；②不同时刻所需的 token 数量差别很大，固定的压缩率或静态重要性指标要么浪费算力，要么丢掉控制关键信息。
方法：FastVLA 是免训练框架，无需重训 VLA。每一步用“任务到视觉”的注意力给 token 打分，再用逆 Simpson 指标衡量重要性分布的均匀程度，据此自适应决定压缩率，并用在线滑动窗口做校准。
结果：在 OpenVLA、OpenVLA-OFT、CogACT 三种模型，LIBERO、SIMPLER 两个仿真基准以及真实 Franka Research 3 机械臂上评测：仿真中 LLM 主干 FLOPs 降低 35–59%，动作延迟降低 9–32%（1.09–1.46 倍加速），成功率保持；真机端到端延迟降低 20%（1.25 倍加速），成功率相当。与现有即插即用的 token 压缩、剪枝、复用基线相比，效率-性能折中相当或更优。
为何重要：它让“看得更全、算得更少”在 VLA 闭环控制中成为现实，且即插即用，便于直接接入已有系统。

rm.usage: 针对 VLA 模型的视觉 token 压缩与推理加速，RoboMaster 目前几乎不使用 VLA 做控制，自瞄/导航也没有大模型主干，关联很弱；仅在探索「大模型直接输出云台/底盘指令」时才有间接参考价值。

items.title_en: Onboard Lightweight LLM Reasoning for Human-Aware Safe UAV Navigation
items.title_zh: 面向人机共融安全无人机导航的机载轻量化 LLM 推理
items.abstract_en: Aerial robots operating near people must treat a pedestrian, a parked car, and a wall differently, yet conventional perception--planning stacks reduce all of them to occupied geometry---a \emph{human-aware safety gap} in which category-specific clearance is unavailable to the planner and temporary occlusions remove pedestrian-specific constraints from its map. We present a modular, fully onboard pipeline that closes this gap by turning visual observations into context-dependent safety constraints for real-time UAV navigation. A shared BLIP encoder drives scene captioning and text-conditioned segmentation, which is fused with depth to localize obstacles in 3D. Obstacle-specific risk is inferred by a lightweight LLM (Qwen-2.5-0.5B) stabilized with retrieval-augmented generation and grammar-constrained decoding that restricts its output to a planner-compatible JSON schema. The LLM reasons once per object category rather than per frame: its verdicts are cached per class, so previously seen categories are resolved without inference and new ones trigger a fresh retrieval-grounded query; detections are additionally given persistent identities and held in the map across occlusions. The perception pipeline runs at 10\,Hz on a Jetson Orin NX, while fallback LLM queries take approximately 0.8\,s and remain off the control-critical path. In Gazebo, low-altitude urban navigation among pedestrians and vehicles shows a roughly $3\times$ reduction in collision events over a geometric planner, and semantics-aware landing among moving actors raises success from 34\% to 96\%. The 224-pixel encoder input limits reliable small-object perception at range; conservative pedestrian margins and short-term persistence mitigate this limitation during navigation.
items.abstract_zh: 在人群附近作业的无人机需要区别对待行人、停放车辆与墙壁，但传统感知—规划流水线把它们一律简化为占据几何，形成“人类感知安全鸿沟”：规划器拿不到与类别相关的安全间距，临时遮挡还会让行人的专属约束从地图中消失。本文提出一条模块化、完全机载的流水线：共享 BLIP 编码器驱动场景描述与文本条件分割，再与深度图融合实现障碍物三维定位；障碍物风险由轻量级 LLM（Qwen-2.5-0.5B）推断，并用检索增强生成与语法约束解码稳定输出，使其只产生规划器兼容的 JSON。LLM 按物体类别而非逐帧推理，结果按类缓存，检测目标具有持久身份以跨越遮挡。在 Gazebo 城市低空导航中，碰撞事件较几何规划器减少约 3 倍，语义感知着陆成功率由 34% 提升至 96%。编码器 224 像素输入限制了远距离小目标感知。
items.highlight_zh: 类别级缓存 LLM 语义约束，碰撞事件减少约 3 倍
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究了什么问题：无人机在人群附近飞行时，必须对行人、汽车、墙给出不同的安全间距，但常规方法把所有障碍都当成“占地方的一块几何”，规划器无法按类别设定安全边界；而且行人被临时遮挡后，其专属约束还会从地图上消失。
2) 用了什么方法：作者搭建一条完全运行在机载设备上的模块化流水线。用共享的 BLIP 编码器同时完成场景描述和“文本条件分割”，再与深度图融合，把障碍物定位到三维空间。风险判断交给轻量级 LLM（Qwen-2.5-0.5B），并用检索增强生成（RAG）加语法约束解码，强制输出规划器能直接读取的 JSON 格式。关键效率设计是“按类别推理”，不按帧推理：同一类物体只询问一次 LLM，结果缓存复用；新类别才触发新的检索查询。检测到的物体还获得持久身份，被遮挡时仍保留在地图中。
3) 有什么结果：整套感知在 Jetson Orin NX 上以 10 Hz 运行，LLM 兜底查询约 0.8 秒，且不在控制关键路径上，因此不会拖慢实时控制。Gazebo 中行人车辆混行的城市低空场景里，碰撞事件比纯几何规划器减少约 3 倍；在移动目标间进行语义感知着陆，成功率从 34% 提升到 96%。
4) 为何重要：它把“物体是什么、该离多远”这类语义安全约束变成了机载实时可用的东西，而不是依赖云端大模型。作者也如实说明局限：224 像素输入在远距离小目标上不可靠，只能靠保守的行人安全裕度和短时记忆来缓解。

rm.usage: 其核心是用轻量 LLM 输出受语法约束的规划器兼容 JSON，并做按类缓存与目标持久身份跟踪。哨兵导航场景较为结构化（无行人语义需求），可直接借鉴的是「LLM 输出结构化决策指令+目标 ID 跨遮挡维持」这一思路，可用于哨兵战术层决策或雷达多目标 ID 保持。

items.title_en: SPEAR: Selective Preference Elicitation with Adaptive Rewards for VLM-Guided Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: SPEAR：面向 VLM 引导机器人操作的选择性偏好查询与自适应奖励
items.abstract_en: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable automated preference labeling for robotic manipulation, yet their deployment remains impractical since each query incurs substantial inference cost, while VLMs frequently abstain on visually challenging comparisons. We propose SPEAR, a framework that transforms VLMs into efficient preference oracles via two synergistic mechanisms. First, we design distinguishability-aware query selection to reduce abstention rates by targeting only informative and distinguishable comparisons. Second, we deploy an adaptive reward transition that bootstraps exploration with VLM-synthesized guidance before preference-based refinement. Experiments on the manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that SPEAR achieves 88.9% average success, outperforming baselines by 23.3 percentage points, while significantly reducing abstention and wall-clock training time on contact-rich tasks. SPEAR learns three Mobile ALOHA manipulation tasks fully online on real hardware, demonstrating end-to-end real-world applicability. By addressing query efficiency and exploration challenges, SPEAR establishes VLMs as practical preference oracles for scalable robot learning without manual reward engineering.
items.abstract_zh: 近期视觉语言模型（VLM）可为机器人操作自动标注偏好，但每次查询推理开销很大，且 VLM 在视觉上难以判断的比较中经常弃答，使其难以实际部署。我们提出 SPEAR 框架，通过两种协同机制将 VLM 变为高效的偏好预言机：其一，设计可区分性感知的查询选择，只针对有信息量且可区分的比较，从而降低弃答率；其二，引入自适应奖励过渡，先用 VLM 合成的引导信号启动探索，再以偏好数据做细化。在操作基准上的实验表明，SPEAR 平均成功率达 88.9%，比基线高出 23.3 个百分点，同时在接触丰富的任务中显著减少弃答并缩短训练实际耗时。SPEAR 在真实硬件上完全在线地学习了三个 Mobile ALOHA 操作任务，展示了端到端的实际可用性。通过解决查询效率与探索难题，SPEAR 让 VLM 成为可规模化机器人学习的实用偏好预言机，无需人工设计奖励。
items.highlight_zh: 平均成功率 88.9%，超基线 23.3 个百分点
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究了什么问题：用人类偏好来训练机器人技能很有效，但人工标注太贵。VLM 可以自动打偏好标签，却有两个问题：每次查询都要付出不小的推理成本；遇到视觉上难以分辨的两段操作时，VLM 常常给不出结论（弃答）。这让 VLM 当“偏好裁判”在工程上不划算。
2) 用了什么方法：SPEAR 用两个互补机制改造这一流程。第一是“可区分性感知的查询选择”：主动挑出既有信息量、VLM 又有把握分辨的比较，从源头压低弃答率，避免把预算浪费在模糊样本上。第二是“自适应奖励过渡”：训练初期先用 VLM 合成的引导信号帮助探索，等偏好数据积累后再切换到基于偏好的奖励细化，缓解纯偏好学习初期信号稀疏、探索困难的问题。
3) 有什么结果：在操作基准上平均成功率 88.9%，比基线高 23.3 个百分点；在接触丰富的任务中弃答率和训练实际耗时都明显下降。除仿真外，作者还在真实硬件上全在线学习了三个 Mobile ALOHA 操作任务，验证了端到端可行性。
4) 为何重要：它把“用 VLM 自动给奖励”从概念验证推进到能省查询、能稳定探索的实用方案，减少人工奖励工程，为可规模化的机器人学习提供了一条现实路径。
items.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at IROS 2026. Project page: https://zevinwu.github.io/spear-project

rm.usage: 用 VLM 自动生成偏好奖励、减少无效查询以加速强化学习训练。可迁移到仿真任务中，为自瞄命中、哨兵走位、多机协同等难以手工设计奖励的行为自动构造奖励函数，属于 RL 训练的支撑性工具。

items.title_en: MR-MPCC: Model Predictive Contouring Control for Robotic Manipulator Tracking under Moving Reference Frames
items.title_zh: MR-MPCC：移动参考坐标系下机器人机械臂跟踪的模型预测轮廓控制
items.abstract_en: Maintaining small path-tracking errors under moving reference frames is essential for robotic manipulation tasks with tight execution tolerances, such as machining and surgical automation. Conventional time-indexed controllers, including tracking Model Predictive Control (MPC), rely on a fixed temporal correspondence with the reference trajectory and may therefore accumulate path-relative error under abrupt reference-frame motion or timing mismatch. This paper presents MR-MPCC, a Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) framework for velocity-controlled robotic manipulators with 6-DoF end-effector pose regulation under Moving-Reference disturbances. A hierarchical control architecture is adopted, in which an upper-level MPCC optimizes path progress while penalizing contouring and orientation errors, and a constrained resolved motion rate control (RMRC) layer maps the commanded Cartesian twist to feasible joint velocities under joint-level and safety constraints. MR-MPCC is implemented in a ROS2--MuJoCo pipeline and validated on a UR5e platform under moving-reference disturbances, where the path frame is perturbed and tracked by electromagnetic sensors. Compared with PI control and time-indexed tracking MPC under matched disturbance, MR-MPCC achieves lower geometric path-following error and smaller deviations in the moving path frame, demonstrating improved path-following performance under reference-frame motion.
items.comment: Accepted by The IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems 2026 (IROS 2026)

rm.usage: 针对移动参考系下路径跟踪误差累积问题的 MPCC 方法，可改造用于云台跟踪高速运动装甲板：以轮廓误差（垂直指向偏差）替代时间索引误差建模，减小目标机动与时延不匹配带来的跟踪滞后，配合弹道预测提升命中率。

items.title_en: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching
items.title_zh: OmniPoser：基于掩码流匹配的野外灵活人体运动恢复
items.abstract_en: Recovering 3D human motion from sparse wearable sensors is challenging due to the inherent noise, occlusion, and instability of real-world tracking signals. Existing approaches are restricted to fixed sensor configurations and, when built on diffusion models, are computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment. We propose OmniPoser, a universal framework that recovers full-body SMPL motion from a flexible combination of heterogeneous inputs, such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, head-mounted 6-DoF poses, or any subset thereof, within a single model. OmniPoser introduces a cross-modal masking mechanism paired with a Masked Conditioning Encoder, enabling one architecture to incorporate diverse sensor configurations through a masked design. A decoupled dual-stream generative backbone generates complete motion via Conditional Flow Matching, requiring only a single ODE integration step at inference. Across three settings and seven benchmarks, including in-the-wild Nymeria and Ego-Exo4D datasets, OmniPoser performs on par with state-of-the-art methods while running at over 700 FPS. The project page is available at https://jamesbridgewater51.github.io/omniposer-eccv/.
items.comment: Accepted as a poster at the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026

items.title_en: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: CocoRNA：基于协作多智能体强化学习的集体RNA设计
items.abstract_en: Designing RNA sequences that reliably fold into specific secondary structures is essential for understanding their biological functions but remains a challenging computational problem. We propose CocoRNA, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for RNA inverse design. CocoRNA simplifies the design task by decomposing it into smaller sub-problems, each solved collaboratively by multiple agents. This approach reduces the complexity of the problem and improves the exploration of design policies. During training, a centralized critic uses global structural information to guide the agents, enabling them to jointly optimize their design strategies. As a result, CocoRNA learns high-quality RNA design policies that generalize effectively to unseen structures without additional training. Experiments on the Rfam dataset demonstrate that CocoRNA substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both success rate and design speed. Further experiments on other biological sequence design tasks highlight the effectiveness and broad potential of CocoRNA for complex design tasks.

items.title_en: CoEvolve: Self-Evolving Code Policies from Skills to Strategies for Humanoid Robots
items.title_zh: CoEvolve：面向人形机器人从技能到策略的自演化代码策略
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) have expanded the manipulation and whole body capabilities of individual robots. Yet a single robot remains limited by its embodiment, and many real world tasks require capabilities that can only emerge through cooperation. Existing multi robot frameworks largely emphasize task decomposition, allocation, and replanning, while providing limited support for adapting executable coordination when physical execution deviates from the intended behavior. We present CoEvolve, a framework that represents team coordination as executable code over fixed robot motor skills. CoEvolve introduces Verifier Guided Coordination Evolution, where a multimodal foundation model instantiates coordination strategies through motion primitives, semantic objectives, temporary robot roles, and bounded execution parameters. Physical verification evaluates each executed transition, rejected behaviors trigger structured coordination revision from an accepted checkpoint, and verified experience is retained to guide subsequent decisions. We evaluate CoEvolve with two simulated Unitree G1 humanoids transporting a freely supported rigid payload through constrained corridors. Across 15 base task runs with three multimodal backbone families, CoEvolve completes 8 tasks, with every backbone achieving end to end success. Additional evaluations yield verified placement on two additional corridor layouts and after both same-backbone and cross-backbone experience initialization, while exposing persistent limitations in motion precision and contact stability. These results support executable coordination as a practical interface for adapting long horizon multi robot collaboration under shared physical constraints.

items.title_en: I2V-DETACH: Source Grounding Detachment for Unauthorized Image-to-Video Generation
items.title_zh: I2V-DETACH：面向未授权图像到视频生成的源接地脱离
items.abstract_en: Recent diffusion models have advanced image-conditioned video generation, but their accessibility raises risks of unauthorized manipulation. Image immunization has emerged as a promising defense for Image-to-Video (I2V) protection, yet existing methods often rely on degrading visual quality or temporal coherence. In this work, we revisit I2V immunization as reducing source-content preservation, shifting the focus from output degradation to weakening source-conditioned content propagation. To this end, we propose I2V-DETACH, an image immunization method that prevents unauthorized I2V generation through source grounding detachment. I2V models preserve source content by propagating source-image cues into video latents during denoising. Accordingly, I2V-DETACH disrupts this process in two complementary ways: it suppresses source-video grounding to reduce source cue propagation, and strengthens intra-video interactions to shift denoising toward video-side dynamics with reduced reliance on the source image. To obtain informative optimization signals, we initialize auxiliary video latents with source-oriented states that remain within the source-conditioned generation regime while deviating from source-preserving trajectories. Extensive experiments across diverse diffusion architectures show that I2V-DETACH substantially reduces source-content preservation, improves over prior immunization methods, and exhibits strong black-box transferability.

items.title_en: Tiered-Resolution Volumetric Mapping for Real-Time Simultaneous Planning and Mapping on Natural Outdoor Environments
items.title_zh: 面向自然室外环境中实时同步规划与建图的分级分辨率体积建图
items.abstract_en: Real-time volumetric mapping for a planning robot is dominated by the cost of integrating and storing information at the finest resolution, yet only a small fraction of any map ever lies on or near a path the planner actually considers. We exploit this with a tiered-resolution mapping mechanism that integrates LiDAR into a single map structure at two resolutions simultaneously: fine inside a corridor around the robot's current plan, and coarse everywhere else. As opposed to traditional navigation pipelines where path planning uses the mapping result and provides no feedback, we propose a feedback loop where planning also informs mapping to dynamically integrate information at different leaf resolutions. Across two real-world teleoperated datasets, replayed and scored offline against an independent full-resolution map, the tiered maps are 13-15x smaller and require 6-8x less integration CPU time than a uniform fine map, while producing paths at a similar cost per meter as the ones generated from fine resolution maps on both scenarios. A uniform coarse map reaches the same size savings but its path quality collapses (+210% cost per meter) on the harder scenario, because it over-discretizes terrain the robot must traverse. Tiering approximates the coarse map's cheapness without its failure mode.
items.comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, IROS 2026 "Data in Field Robotics: From State Estimation to Navigation" workshop

items.title_en: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: LIBERO-PeRM：个性化机器人操作基准评测
items.abstract_en: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.
items.comment: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026); Project Website: https://libero-perm.github.io/

items.title_en: Collective Learning for Unified Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Dynamics Adaptation
items.title_zh: 基于预测动力学自适应的统一机器人操作集体学习
items.abstract_en: Learning a collective policy for state-based Cartesian manipulation across diverse robotic embodiments presents a fundamental challenge due to embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. Collective learning aggregates multi-robot experience to discover shared task structure, yet naive aggregation can average incompatible action modes when different embodiments realize the same Cartesian command through different transition behavior. This leads to strategy ambiguity and performance collapse on dynamically outlying embodiments. To address this, we propose PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that separates shared task-space intent from embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. The first stage employs a representation layer pre-trained on offline trajectories to extract task-level context from collective data. The second stage introduces a decision layer equipped with a predictive dynamics adapter. By forcing the latent state to predict future transitions, this adapter acts as a latent regularizer that grounds the policy in the transition behavior of the executing robot while preserving real-time inference without online planning. Evaluations across simulated embodiments demonstrate that our method prevents performance collapse on distinct robots. It achieves over 93\% overall success and 89\% on dynamically out-of-distribution zero-shot simulated robots, outperforming the Transformer behavior cloning (82\%) and diffusion policy baselines (66\%). Physical KUKA deployment further validates the feasibility of the full state-based pipeline under zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.
items.comment: Accepted at IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)

items.title_en: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments
items.title_zh: 面向北极环境冰下机器人感知的三维重建基准评测
items.abstract_en: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar. While sonar provides robust large-scale geometry, it lacks spectral and high-resolution textural information required to record fine morphological features - a critical limitation in under-ice environments, where sparse visual features and degraded sensing conditions challenge the capture of detailed structural and optical surface properties. We present a benchmark for vision-based under-ice 3D reconstruction using real-world data from the MOSAiC expedition and synthetic data generated in an Unreal Engine-based underwater robotics simulator. The benchmark evaluates Structure-From-Motion (SfM) and monocular depth estimation, with quantitative comparison enabled through cross-modal registration to upward-looking multibeam sonar.
items.comment: Presented at the ICRA 2026 Workshop "From Sea to Space: Advancing Perception in Harsh Domains" (S2S), Vienna, Austria, June 1, 2026. 8 figures, 2 tables. Workshop: https://sites.google.com/view/icra-2026-s2s-perception/

items.title_en: PACT: Posture-Aligned Co-Design Technique for Hand Configuration and Retargeting in Multi-Finger Imitation Learning
items.title_zh: PACT：多指模仿学习中手部构型与重定向的姿态对齐协同设计技术
items.abstract_en: The fidelity of teleoperated demonstrations used for imitation learning is determined by how faithfully a robot hand can replicate the operator's posture. The posture retargeting law that the robot will execute is typically selected only once the hardware has been finalized, and conventional hand designs often neglect human-like grasping postures. We introduce PACT, an optimization based on human grasping postures that jointly optimizes the mechanical parameters of a 17-servo robot hand (link lengths, joint offsets, mounting angles, and base placements) and its nonlinear posture retargeter (a linear human-to-robot joint map, per-joint posture-IK weights, and damping). The optimization enforces full-finger correspondence (MCP, PIP, DIP, and tip of each finger) to human poses from the DexYCB dataset, and is constrained by servo interference, assembly clearances, and flat-hand protrusion, so the resulting design can be physically assembled. We fabricate the PACT Hand and validate it through teleoperation experiments and an imitation-learning demonstration. The hand reproduces all human hand keypoints with a kinematic RMSE of 3.9 mm, compared to 12.8 mm for the LEAP Hand baseline, and keeps all fingertips within 10 mm on every grasping posture, while the baseline achieves this for only 21.6% of the poses. Under matched per-joint torque limits, it lifts twice the baseline payload, 2 kg against 1 kg, and deforms a held paper cup seven times less, reaching a deformation level comparable to a human hand. It also achieves an 86% grasping success rate on YCB daily objects, compared to 64% for the baseline. Finally, as a demonstration, an imitation-learning policy trained on demonstrations collected with the PACT Hand achieved a 75% success rate at held-out placements in a can pick-and-place task. Project page: https://pact-hand-2027.github.io
items.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027. Project page: https://pact-hand-2027.github.io

items.title_en: Intent-guided Adaptive Stiffening for Visuomotor Policies under Unknown Resistance
items.title_zh: 未知阻力下视觉运动策略的意图引导自适应刚度增强
items.abstract_en: Manipulation tasks such as unscrewing a cap or sliding a part in contact with a surface require imposing force along a high-friction direction: the robot must overcome a resistance rather than yield to it. Generative visuomotor policies predict the motion for such tasks but not the authority needed to realize it, and that authority is bounded by the impedance controller beneath them: when the resistance exceeds what a compliant controller can exert under a bounded tracking error, the task is unattainable however accurate the prediction is. The required amount cannot be anticipated either, since it depends on a contact state the observation does not reveal. In this paper, we propose a residual stiffening layer placed underneath an unmodified policy. Resistance is recognized, without force sensing, from the mismatch between the motion the policy commands and the motion the robot realizes, and a four-mode supervisor raises the stiffness along a single direction read off the policy's own action chunk, retains it while the task progresses and releases it afterwards. The layer needs no compliance labels, no retraining and no re-collected demonstrations. On two real tasks, unscrewing a bottle cap and pushing a T-nut along a T-slot groove against non-homogeneous friction, evaluated at six resistance levels of which two were withheld from the demonstrations, the layer raises the success rate from 52% to 90% while producing 61% less peak off-axis force than a uniformly stiff controller at the same resistance.

rm.usage: 研究在阻抗控制下对未知阻力的刚度自适应增强，可作为工程机器人插装/拧紧（如安装42mm发射机构、能量单元）时的力控思路参考，但论文偏通用操作策略，落地需大量改造。

items.title_en: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
items.title_zh: Lean4AgenticRL：以可验证多级过程奖励推进智能体强化学习
items.abstract_en: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.

items.title_en: Improving Policy Learning from Delayed Interventions
items.title_zh: 从延迟干预中改进策略学习
items.abstract_en: In this work, we explore the idea of expert intervention delays in human-supervised robotic systems for imitation learning system. Previous works in imitation learning have primarily examined the impact of suboptimal experts, where the expert policy makes mistakes, but assumed expert interventions occur immediately after errors are made. Although delayed expert intervention can be viewed as a form of noise that might improve policy robustness, our results show that learning from delayed expert interventions is overall less effective than learning from non-delayed expert interventions; delayed expert interventions are less effective at demonstrating error avoidance behaviors. To address this, we propose Learning from Delayed Intervention (LfDI), which learns a cost function based on where and when the expert intervenes, combined with limited information about the extent of intervention delays provided by the expert. This cost function is then used to infer additional supervision for states without expert data, guiding the policy to avoid states that would likely trigger interventions. We evaluate our method, Learning from Delayed Intervention (LfDI), on simulated environments and show that it outperforms other methods that do not account for intervention delays.

rm.usage: 分析专家干预延迟对模仿学习的影响，可提醒遥操作采集自瞄/装配示教数据时及时接管；但结论偏实验性，对赛事算法直接帮助有限。

items.title_en: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
items.title_zh: 盲精确装配：面向多样零件的本体感知 Sim-to-Real 轴孔装配
items.abstract_en: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich assembly, where the robot must find a millimeter-scale opening, mesh gear teeth, or catch a thread through light contact? We study this question by training blind assembly policies that observe only a short history of joint positions, velocities, and their own actions, without visual, force, torque, or tactile sensing. The poses of both the fixture and the part are unknown to the policy, and the grasp is randomized substantially. The policy must therefore assemble the parts through contact, sensed exclusively through its own proprioception. Trained with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts, such policies learn peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading. The peg insertion policy transfers zero-shot to the real world and inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 73% of trials. Controlled comparisons with matched visual policies in simulation show that blind policies generalize far better to unseen part shapes and sizes, though they can be slower. Training such policies needs thousands of different assemblies, each simulated with its clearance intact, so we also release an open-source generator that builds them procedurally from exact convex pieces for MuJoCo; it is more accurate and faster than convex decomposition or MuJoCo's signed-distance collision. Videos and interactive simulations are at https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/.
items.comment: 21 pages, 15 figures, 7 tables. Antonia Bronars and Younghyo Park contributed equally. Project page: https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/

items.title_en: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
items.title_zh: 量子网络中的传输质量估计：计算、仿真还是学习？
items.abstract_en: Future quantum networks will rely on control-plane decisions such as routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. Each decision depends on a timely and reliable estimate of the quality of the entanglement that a candidate path can deliver, with end-to-end fidelity as a central metric. Inspired by the optical-networking experience with quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, this article asks when a quantum controller should compute fidelity analytically, simulate it, or learn a surrogate model. The optical analogy is useful but incomplete: optical QoT estimation often predicts a scalar transmission margin, whereas quantum QoT estimation must account for probabilistic entanglement generation, random memory waiting times, decoherence, state consumption, and measurement constraints that can make fidelity a stochastic target. We propose a compute/simulate/learn framework for quantum QoT estimation and illustrate it with a simulation-based proof of concept. Our study shows that analytical composition can be sufficient in simple regimes, that simulation becomes necessary when stochastic memory effects shape the delivered fidelity distribution, and that lightweight learned surrogates can approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost for online control. We close with open challenges for deployment, including stochastic targets, sim-to-real transfer, data-generation cost, physics-informed learning, and generalization beyond individual paths to full network topologies.

items.title_en: Self-Building Labs
items.title_zh: 自构建实验室
items.abstract_en: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting the role of human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. Project website: https://self-building-labs.github.io/

items.title_en: Not All Actions Contribute Equally: Learning Precise Progress Estimation from Imprecise Demonstrations
items.title_zh: 并非所有动作贡献相同：从不精确演示中学习精确进度估计
items.abstract_en: Progress estimators play an essential role in providing dense reward signals for reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation, but accurately assessing task progress can be much challenging. Existing methods heavily rely on expert data and naively assume that all actions within a demonstration contribute to task success. This assumption often breaks down in real-world scenarios, especially in high-precision manipulation, where subtle geometric errors can lead to task failure. Therefore, these methods can erroneously interpret human mistakes as meaningful progress, further corrupting progress learning. We argue that a key limitation is the lack of a global prior regarding task evaluation criteria, which is crucial for distinguishing meaningful progress from human mistakes. To this end, we propose PRIME, a novel progress estimator capable of learning precise progress estimation from imprecise demonstrations by aggregating experience across trajectories. PRIME constructs a weighted graph over observed states, connecting states across trajectories based on spatial proximity and visual consistency. Edge weights encode spatial distances as transition costs, and shortest-path search approximates the geodesic distance to success. Changes in this distance naturally distinguish advancement, stagnation, and setbacks without assuming monotonic progress over time. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real world on precise manipulation tasks show that PRIME is consistently effective across diverse tasks, and robust to data with varying degrees of suboptimality. Notably, the advantage of PRIME gets more pronounced in higher-precision scenarios, yielding up to a \(5\times\) improvement in policy success rate over the SFT baselines on charger insertion.

items.title_en: Learning Robot Metareasoning: Adaptive Computation Budgets for Real-Time Control
items.title_zh: 学习机器人元推理：面向实时控制的自适应计算预算
items.abstract_en: Planning while moving faces an historical trade-off between deliberation and reactivity. A planner running concurrently with execution needs time to compute, so the robot must commit to an open-loop action chunk for that duration: a longer commitment buys a better plan at the cost of feedback frequency. Existing controllers fix this action commitment, and consequently the computation budget, before deployment. However, the optimal computation time is highly state-dependent (due to factors such as unmodeled dynamics, safety constraints, and marginal optimisation gains), i.e. dynamic, therefore offline static tuning risks leaving systems blind during critical maneuvers or unable to find global effective solutions. We cast the identification of the optimal computation budget as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) in which a single decision defines both the robot action commitments and the time allocated to the solver. To solve this, we train a reinforcement-learning policy conditioned on the current state, the executing plan, and inexpensive planner statistics. Across ground-robot navigation, agile quadrotor flight, and contact-rich manipulation, the learned policy changes its budget with the demands of the scenario, discovering efficient reasoning patterns that outperform fixed-budget baselines. https://lorenzomagnino.github.io/learning-robot-metareasoning-review/

items.title_en: JAXtari: High-Throughput and Easy-to-Modify Arcade Learning Environment
items.title_zh: JAXtari：高吞吐且易于修改的街机学习环境
items.abstract_en: The Arcade Learning Environment (ALE) has been a cornerstone of Deep Reinforcement Learning research, providing a standardized benchmark for evaluating general agents. However, its lack of native support for object-extraction and environment modification restricts research into evaluating whether agents learn robust causal models or rely on brittle visual heuristics. Furthermore, the ALE's dependence on CPU-based emulation creates a significant bottleneck in modern GPU-accelerated training pipelines, limiting both experimental scale and iteration frequency. In this work, we introduce JAXtari, an open-source, high-performance reimplementation of Atari 2600 environments. By leveraging massive GPU parallelization, JAXtari allows PPO agents to finish training on 100M environment steps on a single A100-GPU in under an hour. Beyond speed, it provides object-centric observations and a flexible modification system, allowing researchers to, e.g. develop neuro-symbolic methods or discover novel shortcuts and subsequently train and adapt their agents rapidly, sometimes in only minutes.

items.title_en: Diversity Without Labels: Task-Agnostic Coreset Selection Across Perception and Action
items.title_zh: 无标签多样性：跨感知与动作的任务无关核心集选择
items.abstract_en: While data collection for model training is relatively easy, curating high-quality datasets from large collections is inherently challenging. Coreset estimation methods address this problem by identifying the best data subsets to train models on. However, existing approaches often require proxy model training, extensive annotations, or task-specific tailoring. Unsupervised alternatives typically exploit geometric properties in foundation model feature spaces, but are limited to pairwise image-to-image comparisons or comparisons against a fixed subset. We introduce CoreDNA, an unsupervised, task-agnostic coreset estimation approach that pools neuron activations from vision foundation models into per-image and per-dataset distributions. By comparing each image's distribution to the dataset-level distribution, CoreDNA can capture both low-level visual structure and high-level semantic information across layers. We find that high-quality samples concentrate in the tails of the last layer's activation statistics, which we validate by relating them to training-based coreset methods. Building on these findings, we develop a computationally efficient selection mechanism to construct task-agnostic, high-quality coresets for selective annotation and model training. Across image classification, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and imitation learning for end-to-end driving and mobile manipulation, CoreDNA matches or outperforms the state of the art, demonstrating unprecedented generalization across perception and action tasks. These results highlight the effectiveness of compact activation-based representations for data selection.

items.title_en: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
items.title_zh: 深层 LLM 层揭示默读期间 EEG 中的段落级上下文
items.abstract_en: In a previous report we showed that a decoder can recover open-vocabulary word-level information from 19-channel EEG recorded during silent reading, by aligning short EEG windows with hidden-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model (LLM). That analysis contrasted two of the model's 33 layers: the context-free input embedding and one mid-depth layer. Here we ask how EEG-decodable structure is distributed over the full depth of the language model. We trained one decoder per layer of Llama-3.1-8B, with and without a causal transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. We distinguish word-level decodability from a context-tracking component. Word-level decodability peaks in early layers and declines steadily towards the last layer. In contrast, the context-tracking component of the retrieval gain rises with depth, both with and without a causal transformer. Unexpectedly, a decoder that sees a single 0.5-s window at a time tracks the text passage too. Two new controls dissect this component. A target-geometry control, a synthetic predictor made of the true target plus noise calibrated to each decoder's word-level accuracy, shows that context tracking is not a by-product of word decoding and target geometry. A control that permutes predictions across runs from either the same or from different sessions shows that most of the observed context-tracking is not caused by an EEG recording session signature. Instead, context tracking mostly follows the text. A single EEG window therefore carries passage-level information that a contextual target can absorb. The results locate word identity in the early layers of the language model, discourse state in the deeper layers, and make the choice of target layer a design dial for EEG language decoders.

items.title_en: TransNav: Transformer-Based End-to-End Navigation Method for Static and Dynamic Quadrotor Obstacle Avoidance
items.title_zh: TransNav：基于 Transformer 的静态与动态四旋翼避障端到端导航方法
items.abstract_en: Obstacle avoidance for autonomous quadrotors in cluttered environments remains challenging, especially when both dense static obstacles and moving obstacles are present. Existing methods are often tailored to either static or dynamic settings, which always limit their adaptability across diverse environments. This paper presents TransNav, a transformer-based end-to-end navigation method for quadrotor obstacle avoidance in both static and dynamic environments. TransNav employs a patch-based point-cloud encoding scheme that combines local feature extraction with global contextual modeling, enabling compact yet informative environment representation. The method integrates perception and navigation in a single architecture and directly predicts a finite-horizon action sequence, from which the first action is executed. Moreover, we develop an unsupervised learning strategy by incorporating a lightweight point-mass dynamics model, which directly optimizes trajectory-level costs over the predicted sequence through numerical gradient propagation. Thus, the policy can be efficiently trained without expert demonstrations. Simulation and real-world experiments show that the proposed method achieves strong performance in dense static environments and competitive obstacle-avoidance capability in dynamic scenarios, while maintaining low inference cost for onboard deployment.
items.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

items.title_en: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation
items.title_zh: 基础模型驱动的面向移动操作的三维场景图
items.abstract_en: Geometric and Semantic Foundation models are becoming increasingly popular tools for generating spatial maps for robots. Recent work (e.g., FOUND-IT) has leveraged these tools to construct real-time, task-driven, and open-set 3D scene graphs from a single uncalibrated camera. However, while classical robot mapping techniques have undergone extensive system demonstrations, limited work has been done to develop both the fundamental and the systems wide advancements needed to integrate these new types of robot spatial memory into a full, useable autonomy pipeline. In this paper, we bridge this gap, and in doing so we also evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of this type of 3D memory. Towards this end, we integrate FOUND-IT into a mobile manipulator platform and demonstrate it is well-suited to support multiple objectives such as object change detection, support for multiple mapping sessions, determination of navigable paths, and directly support object grasping for the task of scene re-arrangement. Furthermore, we provide nuanced insights into the effectiveness and limitations of a monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph construction system using observations from rigorous on-robot experiments. Code is available at https://github. com/MIT-SPARK/FOUND-IT.

items.title_en: Enhancing Visual Task-Redirection Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models via Closed-Loop Optimization
items.title_zh: 通过闭环优化增强对视觉-语言-动作模型的视觉任务重定向攻击
items.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable language-guided robot manipulation, but remain vulnerable to visual attacks that undermine user control over robot behavior. Prior studies optimize visual perturbations using fixed target supervision. However, the perturbation can change earlier actions and, in turn, the physical states reached later. As the attacked trajectory evolves, this supervision may no longer match the behavior needed at the states actually reached. Accurately matching these targets can therefore fail to advance the attacker-specified task. Even with suitable supervision, reducing average matching error does not ensure sustained task progress. The robot may still fail at a critical stage, and further updates can disrupt previously successful behavior. To address these limitations, we propose TRACO, a framework that enhances existing targeted visual attacks through closed-loop optimization. Its Execution-Driven Supervision rebuilds supervision for the states reached under attack to guide subsequent updates. Within this framework, Progress-Guided Selection focuses updates where progress stalls while maintaining supervision on the earlier behavior needed to reach that point. Experiments across VLA models and simulation environments show improved task-redirection success with TRACO, highlighting the security implications of closed-loop attack optimization.

items.title_en: Embodiment-Aware Planning for Heterogeneous Bimanual Manipulation
items.title_zh: 面向异构双臂操作的具身感知规划
items.abstract_en: Many manipulation tasks that are effortless for dexterous human hands remain challenging for robotic systems equipped with simple, task-specialized grippers. Industrial platforms commonly rely on end-effectors such as suction cups or parallel-jaw grippers, yet no single mode can reliably satisfy the diverse constraints encountered across different phases of complex manipulation tasks, including pickup, reorientation, insertion, and constrained placement. In this work, we investigate whether complementary simple grippers within a heterogeneous bimanual setup can collectively realize tasks that exceed the capability of any individual gripper alone. Given a single human demonstration specifying the desired object motion, we formulate embodiment-aware execution as a finite-horizon optimization over arm-trajectory assignments. At each segment, the planner determines whether single-arm manipulation or a coordinated dual arm handover is required, jointly reasoning over heterogeneous grasp feasibility, motion constraints, manipulability, and cross-gripper compatibility. Exploiting this formulation, we compute globally consistent assignments with explicit switching regularization. Experiments on a dual Franka FR3 platform equipped with suction and parallel-jaw grippers demonstrate improved feasibility and reliability in tasks that are infeasible under single-gripper execution.

items.title_en: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 面向基于偏好的强化学习的推理引导人类奖励建模
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies optimized for task rewards may produce behaviors that are efficient but misaligned with human expectations, safety preferences, or intent. This paper presents a reason-guided preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) framework that learns a human reward model from trajectory-level feedback. In addition to preference labels, the framework incorporates reason tags explaining why a behavior is preferred, enabling the learned reward to capture both human choices and their underlying rationale. Compared with preference-only reward learning, the reason-guided formulation provides additional supervision for learning human-aligned rewards and improves the interpretability of the resulting policy. The learned human reward is combined with the environment reward during policy optimization, allowing the agent to improve task performance while producing more interpretable, human- aligned, and preference-sensitive behavior

items.title_en: Reinforcement Learning Based Multi-Terrain Adaptive Whole-Body Control for a Quadruped Manipulator
items.title_zh: 基于强化学习的四足机械臂多地形自适应全身控制
items.abstract_en: Legged robots equipped with manipulators offer promising capabilities for loco-manipulation tasks in unstructured environments. However, achieving task-consistent end-effector behavior during locomotion remains challenging due to terrain-induced disturbances and the strong coupling between locomotion and manipulation, particularly for small-scale quadruped platforms. A reinforcement-learning based whole-body control framework is proposed for quadruped loco-manipulation on complex terrain. The proposed framework combines a hybrid task representation with task-prioritized whole-body learning to coordinate locomotion and manipulation while preserving task-consistent end-effector behavior. A lightweight quadruped manipulator platform is further developed to validate the proposed framework on a small-scale quadruped system. Real-world experiments demonstrate successful deployment on complex terrains such as slopes up to 30 degrees, stairs, and deformable terrain. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying learned whole-body control policy for quadruped loco-manipulation in real-world environments and highlight the importance of task-consistent whole-body coordination for terrain-adaptive loco-manipulation.

items.title_en: ReVision: Reprogramming Image Generators for Dense Visual Perception
items.title_zh: ReVision：重编程图像生成器用于稠密视觉感知
items.abstract_en: Recent image generators exhibit rich visual priors that can support dense visual perception. However, existing approaches typically encode multiple perception tasks into a shared parameterization, making joint training sensitive to the mixture and weighting of heterogeneous data and prone to cross-task interference. To address this issue, we introduce ReVision, an instruction-conditioned parameter generation framework built on a frozen multimodal understanding model and a frozen image generator. Given an image and a free-form instruction, the understanding model jointly encodes them into a multimodal image--instruction representation, which a trainable parameter generator maps to transient low-rank updates for the generator. Each image--instruction pair induces a distinct set of transient prediction parameters, enabling instance-specific adaptation while both pretrained backbones remain unchanged. ReVision requires no task-specific heads, explicit task identifiers, or stored adapters. A shared RGB output interface unifies segmentation, depth estimation, and surface-normal prediction. Across diverse dense prediction benchmarks, ReVision achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods while supporting flexible task specification through natural-language instructions. Our analysis further reveals substantial gradient disagreement across tasks, highlighting the conflict introduced when heterogeneous objectives share a single parameterization. Meanwhile, the generated updates exhibit structured task- and input-dependent organization in weight space, further validating instance-level parameter generation for multi-task perception.

items.title_en: FLoTS-SLAM: Optical Flow-Derived Uncertainty for Monocular Dynamic SLAM with Two-Stage Optimization
items.title_zh: FLoTS-SLAM：基于光流导出的不确定性用于两阶段优化的单目动态SLAM
items.abstract_en: Monocular simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) remains challenging in dynamic environments. Real-time dynamic object identification in such environments is a critical problem. Recent approaches estimate per-pixel uncertainty from rendering residuals or multiview feature inconsistency to identify dynamic regions. These methods lack direct motion evidence, and their accuracy may degrade when reconstruction is inaccurate or features are ambiguous. In addition, such uncertainty merely downweights pixels in bundle adjustment (BA), so inaccurate uncertainty estimates can still impair camera pose estimation and 3D reconstruction. Accordingly, we present a monocular RGB SLAM system for dynamic scenes. Specifically, a motion uncertainty estimation method is proposed to derive uncertainty from the residual between optical flow and camera motion induced flow, directly reflecting object motion. The estimation varies with frame alignment accuracy, reducing false detections and yielding accurate pixel-level masks of dynamic regions. To make BA more robust, we estimate camera poses from high confidence pixels. These poses are then used to reproject dynamic pixels during joint refinement of poses and depth, reducing the influence of object motion on both pose and depth updates. Moreover, we provide a quantitative evaluation of dynamic masks and analyze how these masks affect the downstream tracking and reconstruction of dynamic objects. Our approach improves the mean dynamic mask IoU by 35\% over a state-of-the-art baseline on DAVIS, and reduces the average ATE by 59\% on Bonn and 19\% on TUM relative to the SLAM backbone used in our system. The source code will be made publicly available.

items.title_en: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
items.title_zh: HexaShell：探索VLM智能体作为机器人编码智能体边界的轻量框架
items.abstract_en: Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now compete with learned policies on robot manipulation leaderboards. We ask how far a coding agent can go when it controls a robot instead of a computer, and where it stops. Our system, HexaShell, keeps the harness thin: it only turns the agent's commands into robot motion. The agent drives a robot with two arms through one command line. It sees three RGB cameras and knows their calibration. After each failed attempt, the agent reads the log, finds the cause, and writes or fixes small programs called tools. In this way it keeps what it learns as code, as a coding agent does when it fixes a failing test. The tools may use only what the robot observes. They use triangulation to find where objects are, relative to each other and to the gripper. If two cameras see the same point, the point lies where the two camera rays meet. If a point lies on a known plane, such as the table or the top of a block, it lies where its ray meets that plane. When the head camera is not enough, the robot moves a wrist camera to get a second view. We build the tools on only ten layouts of one seed per task, then freeze them and test them on ten new layouts of the same seed. We use Codex with GPT-6-Astra at medium reasoning effort. On all 42 RoboDojo tasks, HexaShell reaches a success rate of 39.7% and a progress score of 48.0, averaged in the same way as the leaderboard. This is a new state of the art on RoboDojo. The limit is contact, not reasoning: pushing reaches 92.5% and memory tasks 65.0%, but tight insertion only 8.3%. When the agent fails, it usually sees the failure but cannot make the motion work. We open source the tools evolved so far at https://github.com/HexaFuture/HexaShell.

rm.usage: VLM 编码智能体通过命令行控制双臂机器人并自我修复工具，和 RoboMaster 强调毫秒级实时自瞄/导航的控制闭环差得远，最多作为调试脚本自动生成工具的启发。

items.title_en: RECREG: Recovery-based Shielding for Regular Safety Properties in Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: RECREG：强化学习中面向常规安全性质的基于恢复的屏蔽机制
items.abstract_en: In many real-world scenarios we need to consider formal requirements, such as safety and constraint compliance, to deploy Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents. In this paper we introduce RecReg, a safe RL framework capable of enforcing non-Markovian regular safety properties via recovery-based shielding. RecReg is a unified approach that supports different levels of a priori knowledge and safety guarantees. The paper primarily focuses on building the theoretical foundations for RecReg in the tabular setting, providing rigorous safety and convergence guarantees that are not present in related work. We provide an extensive set of empirical results using the MASA-Safe-RL library, and we outline an extension of RecReg to deep RL domains using SOTA model-based RL. Our empirical results demonstrate that RecReg achieves efficient learning and matches the theory in this paper.

rm.usage: 安全强化学习的恢复式屏蔽可形式化约束哨兵/决策策略不越界、不违规（如出界、碰撞、误触规则），适合在仿真中训练带安全约束的导航与战术策略；理论以表格环境为主，落地需改造。

items.title_en: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?
items.title_zh: 无眼亦无碍：触觉对盲人保定球操作有何贡献？
items.abstract_en: Humans manipulate objects within their hands through touch alone with remarkable ease, but for robots, achieving sustained real-world manipulation without vision remains an open challenge. Although reinforcement learning (RL) can generate sophisticated blind manipulation policies in simulation, transferring them to a real dexterous hand remains hindered by continuously changing contacts, motion-induced tactile information drift, and the gap between simulated and physical dynamics. We study this problem through Baoding ball rotation on the Shadow Dexterous Hand Lite, using only proprioception and binary tactile feedback as observations. We achieve successful zero-shot transfer through a combination of a sensor-aligned, coupling-aware embodiment in simulation, tactile calibration, and two novel episodic domain randomisations: slew-rate action limits and STuck-AT Taxels. On the physical hand, the policy achieves sustained blind Baoding rotation, completing 225 consecutive $\mathbf{180^\circ}$ rotations (112.5 full rotations) at $\sim0.36 \;\text{rot/s}$ in a single continuous trial without any vision or object-state information. Furthermore, we evaluate the contribution of tactile sensing relative to proprioception alone and identify the hand regions where tactile information is most important. This is the strongest reported hardware result for Baoding ball manipulation in both rotation count and speed, irrespective of the sensing modality used. By effectively bridging the sim-to-real gap, our framework sets a new benchmark for sustained tactile-driven dexterous manipulation on physical hardware.

rm.usage: 仅靠本体感知与触觉做盲操作，而 RoboMaster 工程装配主要依赖视觉标签与位姿估计，且无灵巧触觉手，关联很弱。

items.title_en: AWAM: Active Trajectory-Conditioned View Imagination for Robust Robot Manipulation
items.title_zh: AWAM：面向鲁棒机器人操作的主动轨迹条件化视角想象
items.abstract_en: Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects. However, strong results in structured environments do not automatically transfer to open-world conditions, where clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints can obscure the spatial relationships required for action. To address this perceptual gap, a virtual active-perception paradigm is introduced. AWAM, an Active World-Action Model actively plans where to observe and imagines what will be seen along the planned trajectory before acting. Task-related virtual camera motion is predicted and used as a structured query into a geometry-conditioned world model, producing a reusable spatial prior for manipulation, which is later compressed into a fixed memory and fused with live observations through cross-attention for diffusion-based action prediction. AWAM achieves competitive success rates with 75.9% on LIBERO-Occ, 62.4% on LIBERO-Plus, 76.5% on RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and 94.4% in real-robot trials. These results support improved robustness to the evaluated occlusions and distribution shifts, addressing part of the gap between structured manipulation and less controlled environments.

rm.usage: 主动视角想象可在机械臂抓取/装配前规划观察位姿，缓解遮挡问题，可借鉴到工程机器人装配时的相机/云台主动观察；但 VLA 级模型难以在赛场上实时部署。

items.title_en: Look Before You Act: Bridging Active Perception and Vision-Language-Action Models via Observation-Aligned Data Adaptation
items.title_zh: 三思而后行：通过观测对齐的数据自适应连接主动感知与视觉-语言-动作模型
items.abstract_en: Robots manipulating objects in clutter must decide not only how to act, but also where to look. Although active camera motion can expose an occluded target, it may move the robot into an initial observation-state distribution that differs from the manipulation policy's training distribution. We identify this problem as first-frame distribution sensitivity: under perturbed starts in LIBERO, naively prepending camera repositioning to pi_0.5 reduces success from 46.3% to 11.5%. We introduce ActiveAlign, a data-adaptation framework that trains a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy from the states at which active perception terminates. A learned viewpoint module first generates a camera trajectory. Offline, ActiveAlign uses closed-loop alignment to connect the trajectory endpoint to an existing demonstration, replays the remaining manipulation trajectory, and retains successful continuations for fine-tuning. At deployment, the same viewpoint module precedes the adapted VLA without modifying its architecture. Across 40 LIBERO tasks, ActiveAlign achieves 70.7% success with pi_0 and 72.7% with pi_0.5, outperforming their standard-training baselines by 40.0% and 26.4% respectively. Matched-state and data-matched controls support gains beyond prefix shortening and generic viewpoint augmentation; OpenVLA and GR00T N1 also show the same trend. Success rate under physical occlusion in real world increases from 35/90 to 83/90. These results show that active perception benefits manipulation when policy training is aligned with the observation and robot-state distribution induced by viewpoint selection.

rm.usage: 揭示主动相机运动带来的首帧分布偏移，对工程机器人用云台/底盘先观察再抓取有方法论参考（先对齐观测再执行），但整体是 VLA 大模型框架，直接落到比赛算法上偏弱。

items.title_en: LAW: Unifying Language, Action, and World Modeling for Agentic Physical Intelligence
items.title_zh: LAW：统一语言、动作与世界建模以通向具身物理智能体
items.abstract_en: World-action models jointly predict actions and future world states, but long-horizon manipulation further requires language reasoning to plan subtask objectives, assess execution progress, and guide action selection. We present LAW, a closed-loop VLM--WAM framework that unifies language reasoning, action generation, and world modeling through semantic subtask progress. Within the LAW agent, a hybrid-expert vision-language model plans the remaining subtasks, estimates the values of and fuses actions proposed by a world-action model, and asynchronously assesses execution status to support continued execution and subtask transitions. Within the world-action model, Mixture-of-Transformer Experts integrates modality-specific and shared computation for joint video--action modeling. Dual-stream hierarchical visual memory maintains temporal context for both models, while subtask-local value learning aligns action evaluation with semantic objectives and preserves supervision from successful prefixes of failed trajectories. LAW achieves 94.21% average success across 50 RoboTwin tasks. Replacing the WAM backbone with OpenWAM-$alpha$ further raises the average success rate to 95.56%, establishing a new open-source state of the art on RoboTwin. Despite having only 2B parameters, our VLM also outperforms variants using Embodied-R1.5 and GPT-5.5 High. On three long-horizon real-robot tasks, LAW achieves 65% average success, compared with 28.33% for $pi_{0.5}$ and 25% for Fast-WAM.

rm.usage: 这是一个面向机械臂长时程操作的 VLM+世界模型闭环框架，理论上可用于工程机器人视觉装配任务（科技核心/能量单元安装）的子任务规划与执行进度评估，但模型与算力开销远超机载平台，只能作为算法思路参考。

items.title_en: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation
items.title_zh: SimpleVLN：迈向简单且前沿的视觉-语言导航
items.abstract_en: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to ground language in visual observations and make long-horizon decisions. Existing methods often address these demands through task-specific architectures. As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly capable, an important question remains: Have we truly unlocked the potential of native MLLMs for VLN before introducing task-specific architecture? We present SimpleVLN, an architecture-preserving framework developed through studies of navigation formulation, data construction, and optimization. At the formulation level, SimpleVLN combines single-turn decision inputs with fixed-budget global-local memory to efficiently use navigation history without unbounded context growth, while action chunks enable efficient output of multiple primitive actions per model invocation. For data construction, we combine expert demonstrations with policy-dependent DAgger experience and develop a scalable synthesis pipeline that generates large-scale tasks for reinforcement learning. At the optimization level, a progressive IL-DAgger-RL pipeline advances from action imitation to task-level outcome optimization. Comprehensive experiments validate the effectiveness of these three aspects. We instantiate SimpleVLN across multiple MLLM backbones and model sizes, demonstrating its generality. SimpleVLN achieves 76.7% and 80.1% success rates on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE splits, respectively, substantially outperforming existing methods. These results show that the navigation capabilities of native MLLMs can be effectively unlocked without task-specific architectural designs.

items.title_en: MSC: Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control Framework with Uncertainty-Aware NMPC and RL-based Execution Layer
items.title_zh: MSC：融合不确定性感知NMPC与基于RL执行层的多阶段连铸机感知控制框架
items.abstract_en: Freely swiveling casters are widely adopted in industrial AMRs/SDVs for their mechanical simplicity and load capacity. However, caster misalignment during low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers induces strong contact nonlinearities, widening the planning-execution gap between commanded $(v, ω)$ and realized motion. Existing caster-aware strategies are highly sensitive to state-estimation reliability, causing unstable execution in uncertain transition regimes. To address this, we present Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control (MSC), a planning-execution integrated hierarchical framework featuring two core mechanisms. First, an uncertainty-aware NMPC (CU-MPC) dynamically schedules caster-aware costs and input regularization using predictive uncertainty to suppress overly aggressive maneuvers. Second, a reinforcement learning-based execution layer estimates and predicts caster states under partial observability, transforming high-level velocity commands into physically executable wheel speeds adapted to current contact conditions. Validations in Isaac Sim and real robots demonstrate that MSC offers a clear comparative advantage over existing decoupled compensation approaches by significantly improving caster-state estimation accuracy, minimizing misalignment, and enhancing tracking robustness in caster-sensitive maneuvers.

rm.usage: 可借鉴其不确定性感知 NMPC 加 RL 执行层的分层结构，用于哨兵/步兵在麦轮打滑、定位漂移时缩小规划与执行偏差，提升导航跟线与走位精度。
